issues.failure_explanation: The form $\mathbb{A}_h$ in (s2.10) (and likewise $\widehat{\mathbb{A}}_h$ in (s4.6) and the flux-jump estimator $\eta_{F_\tau}$, which contains $[\![p_h\mathbf{I}-\mu\nabla u_h+u_h\otimes\beta]\!]$) integrates traces of $\beta$ over faces: $[\![u_h\otimes\beta]\!]=(\beta\cdot\mathbf{n}^+)(u_h^+-u_h^-)$ and $\{u_h\otimes\beta\}$ require $\beta\cdot\mathbf{n}$ and $\beta|_F$ on faces. For the stated data class $\beta\in L^\infty(\Omega)^d$ these traces are not defined, and the proofs further bound them in $L^2(F)$ (e.g. (s2.19) estimates $\|h_F^{1/2}\{u_h\otimes\beta\}\|_{0,F}$), which $L^\infty(\Omega)$-regularity does not provide. Hence the construction and the face-term manipulations in the coercivity/consistency proofs are ill-defined or unsupported for the stated class of convection fields. Lemma 3.5 itself restricts to polynomial $\beta$, confirming that $\beta$'s regularity is needed but is not assumed where the formulation and the reliability analysis use it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the assumption on $\beta$ to a class with well-defined $L^2$ face traces (e.g. $\beta$ piecewise $W^{1,\infty}$ or polynomial with respect to a triangulation, as used in the experiments and in Lemma 3.5); all definitions and estimates then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Well-definedness of the DG method (s2.8)-(s2.10), of the equivalent adjoint form (s4.6), of the a posteriori estimators, and of the face-term estimates in Lemma 2.1 and Lemma 2.2r is not guaranteed by the stated hypothesis on $\beta$; the results are only supported for convection fields with well-defined $L^2$ face traces.
issues.title: DG formulation uses face traces of the convection field although only beta in L-infinity is assumed
issues.why_classification: A standard local regularity condition on the input data repairs the defect; the method, all rates, and the advertised scope (the paper's experiments and even its own efficiency analysis already use such $\beta$) survive with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of (s2.80), the second equality in (s2.88) replaces $\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*$ by $\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*-I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*$ and $\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*$ by $\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*-\vartheta_h\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*$ while keeping only adjoint error quantities. It thereby tacitly assumes $\mathbb{A}_h(e_j,I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*)+\overline{\mathbb{B}_h(e_j,\vartheta_h\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*)}=-\mathbb{B}_h(I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*,(\mathbb{S}^*-\mathbb{S}_h^*)u_i^*)$ with $e_j=(\mathbb{T}-\mathbb{T}_h)u_j$. This is false: by the primal Galerkin orthogonality ((s2.26) minus (s2.41), with test $I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*\in\mathbb{X}_h$) and $\overline{\mathbb{B}_h(e_j,q_h)}=0$ ((s2.27) minus (s2.24), with $q_h=\vartheta_h\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*$), the residual equals $-\mathbb{B}_h(I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*,(\mathbb{S}-\mathbb{S}_h)u_j)$, which involves the primal pressure error. The difference between the two sides of the asserted equality is $\mathbb{B}_h(I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*,(\mathbb{S}^*-\mathbb{S}_h^*)u_i^*-(\mathbb{S}-\mathbb{S}_h)u_j)=O(h^s)$, not a higher-order term, so the identity (s2.88) does not hold. (The claimed bound is nevertheless correct: since $\mathbb{B}_h(\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*,\cdot)=0$ for the continuous divergence-free $\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*$, one obtains the valid identity $((\mathbb{T}-\mathbb{T}_h)u_j,u_i^*)=\mathbb{A}_h(e_j,\rho_i^*)+\overline{\mathbb{B}_h(e_j,\sigma_i^*)}+\mathbb{B}_h(\rho_i^*,(\mathbb{S}-\mathbb{S}_h)u_j)$ with $\rho_i^*=\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*-I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*$, $\sigma_i^*=\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*-\vartheta_h\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*$, and each term is $O(h^{2s})$.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rederive (s2.88) via the corrected identity (insert the interpolants, apply the primal Galerkin orthogonality with test $I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*$, use $\overline{\mathbb{B}_h(e_j,\vartheta_h\mathbb{S}^*u_i^*)}=0$ and $\mathbb{B}_h(I_h\mathbb{T}^*u_i^*,\pi_j)=-\mathbb{B}_h(\rho_i^*,\pi_j)$ with the primal pressure error $\pi_j=(\mathbb{S}-\mathbb{S}_h)u_j$), then bound the three terms by $Ch^{2s}$ using (s2.16), (s2.17), (s2.31), (s2.32), (s2.65), (s2.66) and (s2.67). This is a contained repair with no loss of content.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the cluster-average eigenvalue rate $|\lambda-\widehat\lambda_h|\lesssim h^{2s}$ (estimate (s2.80) of Theorem 2.7) rests on an invalid identity; the estimate itself and the remaining claims (s2.79), (s2.81)-(s2.85) of Theorem 2.7 are unaffected, and no other result in the paper uses (s2.88).
issues.title: False identity (s2.88) in the proof of the cluster eigenvalue estimate in Theorem 2.7
issues.why_classification: The proof of a headline a priori guarantee contains a genuinely false equality whose repair requires a contained but nontrivial re-derivation (the middle term must change from the adjoint to the primal pressure error and be justified by orthogonality plus the divergence-free property). Since the stated rate and all other claims survive, it is not serious; since the term's meaning and the inference must be repaired rather than a single symbol fixed, it is not minor.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the reliability bounds (s3.22)/(s3.23) into the eigenvalue identity (s2.78) with $[\mathbf{v}_h,q_h]=[\mathbf{u}_h^*,p_h^*]$ produces, in addition to the estimator and oscillation terms, products involving $\|\lambda_h\mathbf{u}_h-\lambda\mathbf{u}\|_0$ and its adjoint analogue; these enter the derivation but are absent from the statement (s3.33). Eliminating them requires $L^2$-bounds on the individual eigenfunction errors together with an absorption of $|\lambda-\lambda_h|$ into the left-hand side. The paper establishes such $L^2$-bounds only in the non-defective branch of Theorem 2.7 (estimates (s2.81), (s2.83)), a hypothesis that Theorem 3.8 - stated only 'Under the conditions of Theorem 3.1' - does not include, and the one-sentence proof omits the absorption argument entirely. Hence (s3.33) is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to Theorem 3.8 the hypothesis that $\lambda$ is a non-defective (or simple) eigenvalue, and insert the standard absorption: $\|\lambda_h\mathbf{u}_h-\lambda\mathbf{u}\|_0\le|\lambda_h-\lambda|+|\lambda|\,\|\mathbf{u}_h-\mathbf{u}\|_0$, bound $\|\mathbf{u}_h-\mathbf{u}\|_0$ and $\|\mathbf{u}_h^*-\mathbf{u}^*\|_0$ via (s2.81)/(s2.83) combined with (s3.22)/(s3.23), and absorb the resulting $|\lambda-\lambda_h|$-terms into the left-hand side for $h$ small.
issues.overall_effect: The a posteriori eigenvalue bound (s3.33) and, through its citation of Theorem 3.8, the eigenvalue inequality of Corollary cor:added-1 rest on an incomplete argument; under the corollary's non-defectiveness assumption the result is recoverable, but Theorem 3.8 as stated for an arbitrary $j$th eigenpair is not proven.
issues.title: Theorem 3.8 (a posteriori eigenvalue reliability) is asserted without the absorption step and hypotheses its proof requires
issues.why_classification: A headline a posteriori guarantee has its key step essentially omitted and relies on premises established in the paper only under an unstated hypothesis; the repair is contained (a standard absorption plus a hypothesis already assumed in the corollary) and changes no rate, method, or conclusion, so it is not serious, but it goes beyond a local routine patch.
